## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `14487c5027728964e39e56ee0cec56bff9c03d2a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md + skills/objectstack-api/evals/endpoints-auth-routes.json, .changeset/api-skill-delete-recycle-bin.md, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/capture.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/retention.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (runByIdDelete), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-data-writes.ts (deleteData), packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-recycle-bin.object.ts, packages/spec/src/data/recycle-bin.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts (lifecycle class rules), packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts, docs/adr/0148-recycle-bin-separate-store-restore-under-original-ids-retention-in-days.md, packages/skills/scripts/sync-catalog.mjs, ui/scripts/check-skill-eval-tokens.mjs, ui/scripts/skill-bundle-root.mjs

Inputs: card #30847 (body, triage 6679098621, claim comment), PR #30994 (body, two-file list), the net diff at the head against `origin/main` `000a4c0d3` (the merge base IS `origin/main`, so the net diff is the two files and nothing else), and the head's check-runs.

Check-runs at render time: every completed non-skipped run is `success` (Build Core, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · ESLint / PM dispatch-gates / docs & code guards / repo & tooling gates / the three scoped lanes, Type Check · workspace / source gates / debt ledger, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate). Still in progress, not waited on: Test Core (1/8), Test Core (2/8), Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates. No run has failed. Note for the reader of the green `Lint · repo & tooling gates`: `check:skill-eval-tokens` walks `skills/objectui` only (`ui/scripts/skill-bundle-root.mjs`, `SKILL_BUNDLE`), so no gate reads `skills/objectstack-api/evals/**` and a green says nothing about the finding in ④.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept-set changes. The diff touches no schema, no `ApiMethod` / `ApiOperation` enum, no `API_METHOD_DERIVATION` row (`restore` / `purge` stay `flag: () => false`), no `stripLegacyApiMethods` path, no permission key and no route. Every runtime accept set on `main` is unchanged.

The published-surface change is the text of the `@objectstack/skills` catalog. `packages/skills/scripts/sync-catalog.mjs` copies `skills/**` byte for byte into `dist/skills`, so `SKILL.md` and `evals/**` both ship. Each teaching change, judged:

- **L48, route block.** `DELETE … # Delete record (kept in the recycle bin)`. Right for a business object: the REST door's `deleteData` calls `engine.delete(object, { where: { id } })` with no `multi`, which reaches `runByIdDelete` → `openRecycleBinCapture(..., predicate = false)`. Over-broad for the same route on a platform object the data API serves (for example `sys_business_unit`, which is `apiEnabled: true`): `recycleBinTakesObject` refuses every `sys_` / `cloud_` / `ai_` name, so that delete is still physical with no entry. → should-fix S1.
- **L271–272, derived-verb rule.** "`restore` / `purge` never derive: the recycle bin has no restore or purge door yet." Right on `main`. `API_METHOD_DERIVATION` keeps both at `flag: () => false`. The docblock there says they "return as live derived verbs only if/when a real recycle bin ships". No engine restore, purge or REST door exists; `DESTRUCTIVE_OPERATIONS` denies both fail-closed.
- **L411–414, pitfall 2.** Right on every clause it states (see ④).
- **Not changed, but implied by the card:** `evals/endpoints-auth-routes.json` id 5 still grades the retired teaching. This is wrong; see ④ M1.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` matches what the diff publishes. The diff corrects catalog text in a package whose `files` ship `dist/skills/**`. It adds no capability, removes no export and touches no schema, so `patch` is right and `skip-changeset` would have been wrong. The M1 fix lands in the same package and stays `patch`.

`Clause-②: no` is right: no published schema, `packages/spec` surface or governed spec path is in the diff. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing in `packages/metadata-protocol` or the protocol's wire shape moves. The PR body and the changeset carry the same three lines, and `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Contract-review tier waived (PR body, claim).** The dev ran below the tier that `dispatch-gates` mandates for `skills/**`, under the maintainer's standing order of 2026-11-03. This record is the review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, so the tier is served here. Nothing is left to escalate on this point.
- **Partial scope, `Refs #30847`.** Right. The card's Wanted list (who may restore or purge, with which permission, which door) cannot be met while #30237 is open (checked: open). The diff names no door, no grant key (`allowRestoreOwnDeleted` and `manageRecycleBin` are `[PLANNED] … Not read yet` in `permission.zod.ts`) and no route. The card must stay open with `Blocked-by: #30237`, as the claim says.
- **Serial with PR #30844.** That PR edits the same pitfall. The branch merged `origin/main` `000a4c0d` (with #30844), and the net diff against `main` is exactly the three hunks, so #30844's content on `main` is untouched. Resolved.
- **Dropped pointer to `trackHistory` / a `lifecycle` archive.** As a rule this loses nothing that is still true:
  - `lifecycle` retention, TTL and archive are refused on `class: 'record'`, the business-truth class (`object.zod.ts`, ADR-0057 §3.1). An archive is age-based hot-to-cold storage, never an undo of a user's delete.
  - `trackHistory` is a field-change audit trail and gates `history`, which `SKILL.md` L271 still teaches. It does not recover a deleted record.
  - The surviving instruction ("build no soft-delete") keeps the old rule's real content, which was "no custom soft-delete". It agrees with ADR-0148 D1, where the `IsDeleted` shape is explicitly not chosen.
  
  But the drop leaves the skill's own eval grading for the removed words. → ④ M1.
- **Escalation: the claim's file surface.** The claim lists `SKILL.md` (three passages) plus `.changeset/*.md`, "stop on breach". M1's fix is in `skills/objectstack-api/evals/endpoints-auth-routes.json`, which is outside that surface. The dispatching seat must widen the surface, or rule the eval fix a separate change. Either way, the catalog must not ship the corrected `SKILL.md` alongside the uncorrected eval.
- **Tier H approval** (`skills/**`) is still owed by a governed approver. That is outside this record.
- **PR body "Verification" (45 derived commands, exit 0).** This is the dev's account. It is not re-run here (read-only); the head's check-runs above are the verdicts.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md` at the head, judged against `main` and against the bundle's eval scenario for this exact topic.

**True on `main`, each clause of pitfall 2 checked against the code:**

| Clause | Evidence on `main` |
|:--|:--|
| A by-id delete keeps the rows | `engine.ts` `runByIdDelete`: capture → cascade → `bin.write()` → `driver.delete` |
| "a business object's" | `recycleBinTakesObject` = `!hasPlatformObjectPrefix` (`sys_`, `cloud_`, `ai_`). A cascaded platform row is filtered out of the snapshot |
| "rows" | The root plus its master-detail cascade go in one entry (`cascadeMembersInOrder`) |
| `sys_recycle_bin` | `RECYCLE_BIN_OBJECT` |
| "30 days by default" | `resolveRecycleBinRetentionDays`: host resolver, else `OS_RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS`, else `RECYCLE_BIN_DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS` = 30, stamped as `purge_after` and reaped by the `ttl` on `sys_recycle_bin` |
| "never `multi: true` deletes" | `openRecycleBinCapture` returns `undefined` on `predicate`. The engine passes `options?.multi === true`, even on the by-id route the lifecycle reap takes |
| "rows deleted before the bin existed" | ADR-0148 D4 Forward-only. The capture only writes at delete time |
| "Restore is not exposed yet" | No engine restore, purge or empty path. No REST route. Grants `[PLANNED]`. `restore` / `purge` are in `DESTRUCTIVE_OPERATIONS`, so they are denied fail-closed |
| "build no soft-delete" | ADR-0148 D1 |

**No undelivered door is taught.** No route, grant key, `restore()` call or Console page is named. The changeset summary says the same.

**L271–272 inside the derived-verb table.** It reads correctly. "Never derive" is the resolver's present answer (`flag: () => false`). "Yet" does not suggest the verbs become authorable: the next sentence, "Declaring any derived verb in `apiMethods` is stripped at parse with a FROM → TO warning", still governs both. ADR-0148 D5 keeps the retired `apiMethods` values `restore` / `purge` retired. Whether they ever return as derived verbs is #30237's call, and the sentence does not prejudge it. The sentence does not contradict the table above it: neither verb is a table row.

**Findings**

- **M1 (must-fix): the bundle's own eval for this scenario still grades the retired teaching, and the corrected skill now fails it.** `skills/objectstack-api/evals/endpoints-auth-routes.json` id 5 has the prompt "…add … a `restore` operation so deleted invoices can be undeleted". Its expected output is "`restore` / `purge` never derive because DELETE is a hard delete; recoverability is per-field `trackHistory` or a `lifecycle` archive policy". It carries `must_contain: ["apiMethods", "/batch", "trackHistory", "lifecycle"]`. This is the card's defect, word for word, and it ships in `@objectstack/skills` (`sync-catalog.mjs` copies `skills/**` whole). An agent answering prompt 5 from the corrected `SKILL.md` would say the invoice rows are kept in `sys_recycle_bin` and that restore is not exposed yet. The eval marks that answer wrong in two ways: its expected output says the opposite, and `lifecycle` is now taught nowhere in `skills/objectstack-api/**/*.md`, so its `must_contain` token cannot be earned. The fix belongs in this PR:
  - Rewrite id 5's `expected_output` to the new teaching: derived verbs are stripped; `restore` / `purge` do not derive; by-id deletes are kept in `sys_recycle_bin`; restore is not exposed yet; no custom soft-delete.
  - Replace `trackHistory` / `lifecycle` in `must_contain` with tokens the bundle teaches, such as `sys_recycle_bin`.
  - Keep `'restore'` in `must_not_contain`.
  
  No gate catches this: `check:skill-eval-tokens` walks only `skills/objectui`.
- **S1 (should-fix): L48's route comment is unconditional.** The same `DELETE /api/v1/data/{object}/:id` serves `sys_` / `cloud_` / `ai_` objects that have the data API on (for example `sys_business_unit`). Those deletes are physical and enter no bin. Qualify the comment in place, for example `# Delete record (business objects: kept in the recycle bin)`. That stays on one line and costs no budget.
- **S2 (should-fix): naming `sys_recycle_bin` invites a read the data API refuses.** `sys_recycle_bin` is `apiEnabled: false`, `apiMethods: []`: nothing reads it over REST until #30237's doors land. An agent asked "show me deleted invoices" will try `GET /api/v1/data/sys_recycle_bin`. Widen "Restore is not exposed yet" to "Nothing lists or restores it over the API yet". That stays inside the passage's four lines.

Not findings, for the record: the bin exists only when `PlatformObjectsPlugin` registers `sys_recycle_bin`; a composition without it logs `info` and keeps nothing. A delete also drops `secret` columns from the snapshot (ADR-0148 D4). Both are below the resolution of a REST-surface pitfall, and neither makes a sentence false for the standard runtime.

### ① Derived judgments

There are still no accept-set changes. No schema, no `ApiMethod` / `ApiOperation` enum and no `API_METHOD_DERIVATION` row changed; `restore` and `purge` stay at `flag: () => false`. No permission key and no route changed.

The published-surface change is the text of the `@objectstack/skills` catalog, where `sync-catalog.mjs` ships all of `skills/**`. Each change is right on `main`:

- **L48, route comment:** `# Delete record (business-object rows → recycle bin)`. Right. The REST door's `deleteData` sends `where: { id }` with no `multi`, which reaches `runByIdDelete`. `recycleBinTakesObject` takes only names outside `sys_`, `cloud_` and `ai_`. The changeset prose now names both the eval change and the "nothing lists or restores it over the API yet" teaching, and it matches the tree. Lines 44–53 of the eval change in place, and no other case moved. The previous record's escalation is resolved.
- **Partial scope, `Refs #30847`.** Still right. #30237 is still open (checked), and the tree names no restore or purge door, grant key or route. The card must stay open with `Blocked-by: #30237`.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md` at the head, judged against `main` and against eval case 5, the bundle's scenario for this topic.

**M1: resolved.** Eval case 5 at the head:

- **`expected_output` is true on `main`.** It says `restore` / `purge` never derive. It says a by-id delete of a business object already keeps its rows in `sys_recycle_bin`, but nothing lists or restores them over the API yet, so there is no restore operation to add and no custom soft-delete to build. Each clause holds:
  - `flag: () => false`.
  - capture in `runByIdDelete`, with `recycleBinTakesObject` limiting it to business objects.
  - `sys_recycle_bin` is `apiEnabled: false`, `apiMethods: []`.
  - there is no engine restore or REST door; `restore` and `purge` are in `DESTRUCTIVE_OPERATIONS`.
  - ADR-0148 D1.
- **`must_contain`** is `["apiMethods", "/batch", "sys_recycle_bin", "recycle bin"]`. Every token is taught by the corrected bundle markdown:
  - `sys_recycle_bin` at L412.
  - `recycle bin` at L48, L272 and L412.
  - `apiMethods` and `/batch` as before.
  
  Multi-word tokens are an established shape across the catalog's evals (99 of them), so `recycle bin` is gradable.
- **`must_not_contain`** still holds `'restore'` and `'search'`.
- The file parses as JSON.
- An agent answering prompt 5 from the corrected `SKILL.md` now satisfies the eval, not the reverse. The phrases "DELETE is a hard delete", "trash surface" and "no recycle bin" no longer appear anywhere under `skills/**`.

**S1: resolved, and still true.** See ①. The comment now limits the bin to business-object rows on a by-id route. That is the exact reach of `openRecycleBinCapture`.

**S2: resolved, and still true.** "Nothing lists or restores it over the API yet" matches `sys_recycle_bin`'s `apiEnabled: false` / `apiMethods: []` and the absence of any restore or purge door. An agent is no longer pointed at a `GET /api/v1/data/sys_recycle_bin` that the data API refuses.

**Pitfall 2, re-read whole.** "Treating `DELETE` as final or as restorable. A by-id delete keeps a business object's rows in the recycle bin (`sys_recycle_bin`, 30 days by default; not `multi: true` deletes, platform rows or rows deleted before the bin existed); nothing lists or restores it over the API yet. No soft-delete." Every clause holds against the code read in the previous record, none of which moved:
- retention resolver → env → 30, stamped as `purge_after`.
- the `predicate` refusal for `multi: true`.
- `hasPlatformObjectPrefix`.
- ADR-0148 D4, forward-only.

No undelivered door, grant or route is taught.

**L271–272** still reads correctly inside the derived-verb table. "Declaring any derived verb in `apiMethods` is stripped at parse" still governs `restore` and `purge`.

**Findings: none.** No must-fix and no should-fix remains.

One note, not a finding. "Over the API" is narrower than the truth on `main`: no engine-level restore exists either. Nothing the sentence states is false, and an agent reading it is not sent to a door that exists elsewhere. The note is recorded only so that the #30237 follow-up rewrites this sentence when the doors land.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [42259097933](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42259097933) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。
